newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Societe Generale opens branch in Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Societe Generale opens branch in Bulgaria.

text.p: France's biggest private bank Societe Generale on Tuesday opened its first branch in Sofia to service corporate clients operating in Bulgaria, a bank official said.

"Societe Generale in Sofia will operate as a commercial bank and we hope that we will be able to increase our investment activities as the Bulgarian economy recovers," Robert Franck, general manager of the bank's Sofia branch, told a news conference.
The opening of the branch coincides with the first week of operation of a fixed exchange rate regime known as a currency board, which Bulgaria introduced on July 1 to stabilise the currency.
"The more economic stability we have the better will be our operation," said Franck.
The bank offers domestic and international banking, but its license restricts it from operations in local government securities, said Franck.
Societe Generale is the second French bank to set up office in Sofia and the ninth foreign one.

Banque Nationale de Paris and Germany's Dresdner Bank AG set up BNP-Dresdner Bank (Bulgaria) AD two years ago, in which BNP and Dresdner hold 40 percent each and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has the remaining 20 percent.

Societe Generale, which posted a 4.5 billion French franc profit in 1996, has opened more than 20 branches in Central and Eastern Europe as part of its expansion in emerging markets. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom +359-2-981-4145
